text:
jamie: quick question — i'm rethinking our collector topology. instead of per-tenant pipelines, what if we do per-signal+namespace pipelines (e.g. spans:serviceA, spans:serviceB, metrics:*, logs:*)? thoughts?

riyad: per-signal makes routing simpler and lets us apply different retention/aggregation per signal. main worry is duplication of processors (sampling/attrs) across many pipelines = memory + CPU. :thinking:

marisol: agree on routing, but we also need per-tenant quotas enforced early. gateway vs agent changes how we apply quotas. agent-side sampling reduces traffic, but gateway centralizes policy.

lex: honestly prefer a hybrid: agent does lightweight prefix sampling + tagging, gateway runs heavy processors + exporters. that keeps east-west traffic down but centralizes expensive steps.

jamie: that aligns with one of my proposals. quick config sketch for per-signal pipelines (pseudo):
```yaml
service: collector
pipelines:
  spans/service-A:
    receivers: [otlp] 
    processors: [resource, span-sampler, batch]
    exporters: [jaeger, retention-router]
  spans/service-B:
    receivers: [otlp]
    processors: [resource, span-sampler, batch]
    exporters: [zipkin, retention-router]
  traces/shared-sampling:
    receivers: [otlp]
    processors: [probabilistic_sampler]
    exporters: [gateway-policy]
```
spam: not a real config, just idea.

riyad: nice. couple of follow-ups: how do we avoid duplicating heavy processors? can we factor processors into a shared component and reference them? otel collector allows pipelines to share processors but runtime instances still allocate resources. Also exporter fan-out: retention-router should be able to route to different retention tiers (hot/cold) based on namespace tags.

marisol: for quotas, we need a policy that can live in gateway and be pushed to agents for pre-filtering. API design: something like /v1/quota-policies that returns sampling + rate limits per namespace. agents pull and apply a cheap token-bucket. gateway does strict enforcement.

lex: UX for rollout: we need a canary flag per-pipeline in console. devs should be able to toggle pipeline-level sampling and see a live delta in token-level cost dashboard. without that it's scary to flip sampling configs.

jamie: +1. we should emit a metric from collector: collector.pipeline.<name>.effective_sampling and collector.pipeline.<name>.ingested_tokens so the console can show potential cost impact before/after.

ci-bot: deploy-bot: staged collector build with new retention-router merged to staging at 1795504450 :white_check_mark:

riyad: timeline? can we prototype with 1-2 high-volume services only (service-A, service-B) and keep others on per-tenant pipelines for now?

marisol: prototype plan:
- stage: implement retention-router in gateway + simple sampling policy API
- agent: implement policy pull + cheap probabilistic sampler
- backfill metrics for cost dashboard (sampling impact)
- run for 2 weeks, compare cost + p99 latency impact

jamie: sounds good. action items: @lex can you mock console toggle + dashboard widgets? @riyad can you own retention-router impl and memory profiling? @marisol can you design policy API and migrations? i'll wire up the prototype configs and test harness.

lex: on it. i'll put a small mock in the console repo and schedule a quick sync next wed.

riyad: i'll start a perf run with 2 pipeline replicas and capture memory/cpu.

marisol: i'll draft the API and send a short spec in this thread by EOD.

jamie: great. tagging this for follow-up in eng-telemetry sync. :thumbsup:
